item.title: The live flow map
item.description:
Since relay v0.2.0.

wctr-relay flowmap --class <class> --url <the relay's https address>

prints a link; open it on the projector. Each student is a box holding their containers, coloured by security group. Each flow is a line between two containers whose width follows its throughput. A refused flow is a dashed red line, and the event log beside the map says which rule was missing (“no ingress rule of … allows it”). Click a container for its address and groups, or a flow for its counters and the rules that allowed it; the arrow keys move from container to container. The filter box dims everything that does not match a student, a container or a group.

Who can see what

Viewer Credential Sees
The teacher the link from wctr-relay flowmap: a read-only ticket in the URL fragment (never sent to a server, removed from the address bar when the page loads), valid 12 hours the whole class
A student their own session token (#class=…&session=…) only the flows that touch their own containers, and the containers at the other end

The ticket allows watching that class’s map and nothing else: it cannot change a rule, list the groups, or join the class.

How it works

The relay aggregates its flow log per edge — source container, destination container, protocol and port — and streams one update per tick (4 per second) over FlowLogService.WatchFlowMap, a server stream of the Connect protocol. A slow page gets the newest map, never a backlog. An update holds at most 400 containers, 2 000 flows and 200 events.

The page is a Go WebAssembly application built on go-widgets’ GraphView (a node-link graph over a view model, added to go-widgets for this page and reusable elsewhere) and LogView. The relay serves it itself, under a strict Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; connect-src 'self' — no inline script, nothing loaded from anywhere else, so it works on a classroom LAN with no internet.

Getting a binary that has it

The page’s WebAssembly is about 5 MB, so it is not in the repository: the binaries attached to each release carry it. From source:

go run ./internal/buildflowmap
go install -tags flowmap ./cmd/wctr-relay

A plain go install …@latest serves the page, which then says the map is missing from that build.

Not yet

Pause and replay of the last minutes; the relay keeps the last 1 000 events, the page shows the last 200.
